facts.raw_span: A 75-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection 10 days after revision surgery
hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and folate deficiency
pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L
A 75-year-old Caucasian woman was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection 10 days after revision surgery
hypertension, type 2 diabetes, heart failure, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and folate deficiency
pulse 80/min, respiratory rate 24/min, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air
Sodium 142 mmol/L, potassium 3.5 mmol/L, chloride 118 mmol/L, bicarbonate 5 mmol/L
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.18, pCO2 1.7 kPa, pO2 16.7 kPa, bicarbonate 8.3 mmol/L, base excess –22.7 mmol/L

concepts.why: The patient has a history of type 2 diabetes and presents with metabolic acidosis, as evidenced by the low bicarbonate level and high anion gap.
The patient's arterial blood gas shows a high anion gap and low bicarbonate level, consistent with lactic acidosis, and the lactic acid level is elevated.
The patient was admitted with a prosthetic hip infection and has a high respiratory rate, consistent with sepsis.
The patient has a history of chronic kidney disease, as evidenced by the baseline creatinine level.
The patient is taking vancomycin and has a history of chronic kidney disease, which increases the risk of nephrotoxicity.
The patient has a high respiratory rate and the arterial blood gas shows a low pCO2 level, consistent with acute respiratory acidosis.
It explains the Glasgow Coma Scale score of 12 in the context of the patient's complex metabolic and respiratory acidosis.

rationales.F01: Prosthetic hip infection may be related to sepsis.
rationales.F02: Chronic kidney disease is a known condition.
rationales.F04: Drowsiness, confusion, and disorientation may be related to various conditions including diabetic ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, and mixed acid-base disorder.
rationales.F10: Arterial blood gas results indicate acidosis, which may be related to diabetic ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, or mixed acid-base disorder.
rationales.F11: Corrected anion gap is elevated, which may indicate lactic acidosis or mixed acid-base disorder.
rationales.F12: Lactic acid level is within normal range, which may rule out lactic acidosis.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation with a high anion gap, metabolic acidosis, and respiratory alkalosis (as evidenced by the low pCO2) suggests a mixed acid-base disorder, which can explain the combination of findings. Lactic acidosis is also a consideration but the lactic acid level is not significantly elevated.
